children: The S&P Global Eurozone Composite PMI came in at 52.0 in August 2026, broadly in line with the preliminary estimate of 52.1 and little changed from July’s eight-month high.

The latest data point to another solid quarter of growth in Q3, supported by improving industrial activity and a recovery in services following the initial impact of the surge in energy prices at the start of the Middle East conflict.
New orders increased at the same solid pace as in July, while new export orders rose for the first time in four and a half years.
Employment also expanded for the first time this year, although backlogs continued to decline at a slower pace.
Inflationary pressures were broadly stable, with input costs easing slightly while output prices rose at the same pace as in July.
However, price pressures remained elevated by historical standards.

title: Eurozone Private-Sector Growth Holds Firm in August
